results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All ten outline summaries state the controlling idea of the spec paragraph they are aligned to (p01 to p10); the callout is page format.
Introduction ¶3: thesis statement plus roadmap is the single controlling idea of p03 by the spec's design; not two ideas beyond the spec entry.

Chapters in this part ¶2: synthesis, reading advice and hand-off are what the spec assigns to p10 and the conclusion; the controlling idea (one line of reasoning that starts with chapter 1) covers them.
Every unit traces: ¶1-¶3 set up and state the part thesis; p04 P1-1; p05 P1-2/3/4; p06 P1-3/4; p07 P1-5; p08-p10 all five as one line of reasoning.

Each scenario and list is followed by what it shows: the same queue for new managers (p01), the failure outliving the person blamed (p02), one explaining sentence per mechanism (p05), capacity added away from the constraint (p06), no stated outcome so the board could not be answered (p07), a reason for each of the two placements (p08).

Pass at eight boundaries: p01->p02 ('That answer goes against a habit'), p02->p03 ('Part I is about what stays in place'), lead->the-claim, p04->p05, p05->p06 ('follows from the three mechanisms'), the-claim->the-second-lens ('A system is built for someone'), reading-order->conclusion list, p09->p10 ('Read in order, the five answers are one line of reasoning'). The hand-off carries the claim and introduces what the structure consists of, as declared.

results.draft_locus: Why the Chapters Come in This Order ¶1
results.quote: The chapters are in prerequisite order: each one supplies the terms the next one needs.
results.finding: The declared transition is a sequence that carries over 'the two lenses' and introduces the order in which five chapters build them. The opening sentence starts on the chapters with nothing carried over from the two sections just read: it does not say that the system claim and the users claim are what the five chapters build. The link rests on the heading and on the roadmap in the lead only. Neither flow reader was stopped by it, so the effect on the reader is small.
results.waived_by: Author (Željko Obrenović), 2026-11-19, decision 'waive by rule': this short part introduction had one check round by the lead session's choice; the unit was revised after it to address this finding and was not re-checked by fresh readers.

results.quote: What that structure consists of, four elements, four things a leader can design and three scarce capacities, is where the first chapter starts
results.finding: Both flow readers were left unsure here. The page has defined structure as three things (boundaries, interfaces, decision rights) and has said 'one scarce capacity at a time'; 'four elements', 'four things a leader can design' and 'three scarce capacities' then arrive as three unexplained counts that seem to contradict what the page just said. The reader cannot tell what the fourth element is, how elements differ from designable things, or how three capacities relate to the one constraint. The spec asks for these three items in the hand-off but does not forbid a clause that names them or ties them to the three parts already given.
results.corroborated_by: flow-b item 2 (rated a); flow-a item 2 (rated a)

results.quote: Read in order, the five answers are one line of reasoning. The arrangement of teams shapes the product, the size of what a team owns limits what it can do well, the slowest step sets the pace of all of them, and the whole is judged by what it does for its users.
results.finding: The sentence announces five answers 'read in order' and gives four, with users last, directly after a section that argued for placing the users chapter second and a list that has it second. Flow reader A went back to the list (a); flow reader B resolved it in place (b), so it is not corroborated. The wording and the order are the spec's synthesis text almost verbatim, so the difficulty comes from the spec.

results.quote: its output is limited by one scarce capacity at a time
results.finding: 'One scarce capacity at a time' is not tied to 'the constraint' when the constraint is introduced in the third mechanism, so the reader has to infer that they are the same thing. Flow reader B rated it (a), flow reader A (b, resolved by reading on), so it is not corroborated. The spec's audience knows the three scarce capacities from the preface, which lessens it; a clause at 'That step is the constraint' would close it.

results.finding: Every working term on does_not_know that the page uses is glossed where it first appears (lead time, boundaries, interfaces, decision rights, Conway's Law, cognitive load, constraint, users, outcomes, discovery); fracture plane and team state are not used. 'Launch requests' and 'jobs' belong to Corvane, which the audience knows in outline; both flow readers resolved them in place.
Opens on a concrete, dated question about Corvane and answers it; no placeholder, dictionary or dawn-of-man opening.
The closing paragraph synthesizes, calls back, advises and hands off; the 'four elements' are the hand-off's announcement of chapter 1, not a new subtopic argued here.

Synthesis present (one line of reasoning); so-what present as what the reader can do (explain Corvane's slowdown without blaming a person or a team). The 'diagnose before replacing people or adding headcount' half of the so-what is stated in p06, not repeated in the closing.
'you can say why new managers would have found the same queue' returns to the opening question.
The intro reader predicted the system half, the users half, then the reading order with the five questions in order: all three roadmap promises.

The AC-1 reader named the five chapters' subjects in reading order, matching the expected answer: system and what a leader can design; product with users and outcomes; Conway's Law; cognitive load and boundaries; flow and the constraint.
